ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First look at the image: The figure shows a triangle and a circle overlapping each other. Part of the circle is inside the triangle, and part extends outside the triangle, so the union of the whole figure can be divided into three non-overlapping parts: the overlapping part of the triangle and the circle, the part with only the triangle, and the part inside the circle but outside the triangle. The problem gives that the overlapping part accounts for 45% of the area of the total figure, and the part of the triangle outside the circle accounts for 40% of the area of the total figure. Therefore, the part inside the circle but outside the triangle accounts for 100% - 45% - 40% = 15% of the total area. The whole circle consists of the overlapping part 45% and the part of the circle outside the triangle 15%, so the total area of the circle accounts for 45% + 15% = 60% of the area of the total figure. What is sought is the percentage of the circle occupied by the part of the circle outside the triangle, namely 15/60 = 25%.

raw_record.question_text: The area of the intersection of a triangle and a circle is $45 \%$ of the total area of the diagram. The area of the triangle outside the circle is $40 \%$ of the total area of the diagram. What percentage of the circle lies outside the triangle?

method.method_draft: First read the image as a triangle and a circle whose union is divided into three non-overlapping visual regions: triangle-only, circle-only, and their overlap. From the text, assign the overlap/intersection as 45% of the total diagram area and the triangle-only region as 40%. Since these regions plus the circle-only region make 100% of the diagram, compute circle-only area as 100% - 45% - 40% = 15%. The whole circle consists of the overlap plus the circle-only part, so its area is 45% + 15% = 60% of the diagram. The requested percentage is 15/60 = 25%.
